learning_outcomes.text: Explain the fundamental elements of European culture and civilization.
Compare the stages that the European continent has gone through from antiquity to the present.
Define notions of culture and civilization.
Describe the stages of the European Union's formation.
Explain the advantages/disadvantages of Romania's accession to the European Union.
Utilize digital tools for presenting specialized works.
Plan the stages of drafting a report that addresses a subject related to the course topic.
Operate with concepts specific to this discipline.
Critically evaluate the advantages/disadvantages of the European Union's formation.

Respect ethical principles, norms, and values in the correct and timely execution of professional tasks, by adopting a rigorous, efficient, and responsible work strategy in decision-making for problem-solving.
Integrate into a workgroup and apply effective relationship and teamwork techniques in multidisciplinary teams, across various hierarchical levels.
Permanently inform and document oneself in one's own field of activity by appropriately using efficient learning methods and techniques throughout life.

syllabus_topics: Culture and Civilization: concept and historical evolution
From the Europe of nations to the European Union
Culture, religion, and art in European civilization
The modern world system
Why democracy?
Theories of modernity
Romanian civilization, European civilization
Engineering and civilization
Culture in the service of European unity
The genesis of the European Union
Romanians and the European Union
Humanistic culture, scientific culture, technological culture
Urban and rural in the civilization of Europe
The future of the European project
Europe between Greek and Roman civilization
Christianity, the connecting element between antiquity and the Middle Ages
European culture and civilization between medieval and modern
Europe of revolutions and their role in shaping the old continent
The role of art in the process of building European culture
From the Europe of nations to the European Union
Romania and Europe
teaching_methods: Discussions based on Power Point presentations
Discovery learning facilitated by direct and indirect exploration of reality

assessment_methods.method: Systematic observation of students (individual/team assignments, report preparation)
Formative evaluation test (checks during the semester)

assessment_rules: The final grade is determined by the weighted scores of each activity within the discipline. Grades are awarded from 1 to 10. A minimum grade of 5 is required to pass the course and obtain credits, certifying the acquisition of minimal learning outcomes. Students must know the main periods of European culture, define culture and civilization concepts, analyze the Church's role in European culture and civilization, present characteristics of the Renaissance and Enlightenment, explain the historical significance of key dates for European and national history, critically analyze the advantages/disadvantages of the European Union's formation, and draft/present a paper on a course-related topic.
